title: Responsibility as part of work organisation

blocks.heading: Responsibility as part of work organisation
blocks.text: Work organisation can give staff meaningful responsibility through delegation, team decisions and job enrichment, or remove discretion by centralising decisions and narrowing tasks. Responsibility should be matched with authority and resources. A wide span of control may leave subordinates more independent if managers delegate appropriately, but a headcount alone does not prove they have authority. A narrow span can support close supervision and development but can also become restrictive if every routine decision needs approval. Staff differ in readiness and desire for responsibility. Give support and clear boundaries, then review outcomes instead of equating less supervision with abandonment. Job enlargement adds tasks at a similar level; enrichment adds meaningful responsibility or challenge, so more repetitive duties alone need not motivate.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Hena Repairs lets competent technicians choose routine repair methods within agreed safety and spending limits, rather than seek approval for each step. Genuine discretion can provide achievement and faster service. The owner retains oversight and must check competence; merely assigning more jobs without decision rights would not create the same responsibility.
